name: gp-judge-v1
description: Golden Path (GP) vibecoded-project judging. Panel-only, one round, five independent labs each answer MET/FAILED against the published rubric (~/Projects/GP/rubric.json) with quoted evidence. Invoked with --draft <dossier> --rounds 1 so the criteria stage, skeleton/proposal/debate stages, and the builder/reviser never run - only the panel critiques the dossier once. Chain data only; no new relay stage type.
criteria: The submitted live URL, or a URL described in the README, loads and renders something within a few seconds (not a blank page, a build error, or a 404).
What loads is an interactive thing (a game, app, tool, or demo the visitor can do something with), not a static description of an idea.
The interface or output is visually coherent: no obviously broken layout, unstyled default HTML, or placeholder Lorem-ipsum-style content.
No visible runtime errors, broken links, or crashes are observed during the judge's brief interaction with the live URL.
The submission reads as a finished small thing rather than an abandoned half-built scaffold (e.g. has a title, a clear entry point, no dangling TODO screens).
The description or README states a clear creative or personal intent behind the project (why it was made, what idea it explores), not just a generic feature list.
The submission has at least one distinctive design or content choice (a theme, joke, aesthetic, or mechanic) that isn't a generic unmodified template or tutorial clone.
The README or description names the AI tools or models used to build the project (e.g. Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or 'vibecoded with X').
The README or description gives at least one concrete detail about the build process (a prompt approach, a workflow step, or a specific decision made during building), beyond just naming a tool.
If a repo URL is given, it is publicly reachable and contains a README.
If a live URL is given, it is publicly reachable without a login wall or paywall blocking the judge's view.
_maxTokensNote: Bumped critics 4000->8000 2026-09-13: 11 rubric criteria means a full criteria+failures reply routinely needs more than 4000 output tokens, and cheap critics (esp. glm-5.3-flash) were hitting stop:length mid-JSON and getting scored as an unparseable abstention rather than a real verdict, confirmed against real panel-1-*.md files that were cut off mid-string. The fix belongs here, not in the judging pipeline that supplies the dossier - the critic maxTokens budget is entirely this chain config. A re-run after the bump came back with every active critic fully parsed, zero abstentions.
